scores.evidence: Managed Instance changes authentication, DNS-alias behaviour and failback rules (failback only works from SQL Server 2022)
scores.rationale: Claims about log shipping with NORECOVERY tail backups, Basic vs full availability groups, ExpressRoute lacking default encryption, MACsec requiring ExpressRoute Direct, and MSH-10 idempotency are all accurate, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: A database that only one place can write to can't switch locations with literally zero interruption
scores.rationale: It resolves the 'no downtime' ambiguity honestly with a ≤15-min write pause requiring clinical sign-off, covers all implied capabilities, and lists explicit, justified exclusions and a fallback if zero is mandated.

scores.evidence: Booking integrity (no double booking) stays in the app's existing database transactions, which we don't touch.
scores.rationale: Single-writer rule, data ownership table, sticky-session handling and the one-way sync choice are honored consistently across flows, cutover steps, rollback and decisions with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: Spike: hidden dependencies (30 days) ... Changes the plan if: we find clients that hard-code IPs
scores.rationale: Riskiest assumptions get early spikes with explicit plan-changing triggers, rehearsals have measurable exit criteria, baselines are measured rather than invented, and the synthetic probe continues validation in production.

scores.evidence: Everything about the current system below is an assumption, numbered A1–A14 in Section 5.
scores.rationale: Every design-bearing assumption is explicit with impact-if-wrong and a validation task and date, and unsupported figures are consistently labeled as assumptions or estimates.

scores.evidence: Duplicate HL7 message when the queue is released ... the engine's duplicate filter is turned on for the 2 hours around cutover.
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures—double-booking, HL7 loss/duplication, double-running jobs, WAN loss, time-zone drift, ransomware, hidden dependencies—each with concrete detection, containment and a specified recovery path.

scores.evidence: Alerts, each with a runbook in runbooks/ ... Same owners as today. The infrastructure on-call team covers VMs and network, the DBA covers SQL
scores.rationale: Domain-meaningful probes and alerts, IaC with what-if gates, named incident ownership, retained hospital tooling (SCCM, EDR, SIEM) and runbooks are sized realistically to the stated small team.

scores.evidence: Production runs at about $5k–15k/month ... The biggest variables are SQL licensing (close to zero with Hybrid Benefit, A12) and Log Analytics ingestion.
scores.rationale: Run costs are a labeled range with components, dominant variables and concrete controls (log caps, budget alerts, reserved instances), dual-run cost and build effort (team, 4.5–7 months) are both covered.

scores.evidence: Point of no return | Reverse sync is stopped on day 30 (M5). Cloud SQL must stay on the same version until then
scores.rationale: Every decision carries a reversibility rating and revisit trigger, the one-way point is explicitly dated, 30-day no-data-loss failback is maintained, and hard-to-reverse choices (D4, D5) get the most scrutiny.

scores.evidence: Copy across, don't rebuild ... Moving to a managed database or containers. This is listed under Deferred Work.
scores.rationale: A minimal rehost with deliberate shortcuts (NSGs only, route-back internet, same engine version) and an explicit deferred-work list; every component is justified and nothing essential is cut.

scores.evidence: T1/T1b/T1c, T2, T3 and S3 start day 1. T4→T5→T6/T7/T8. T9–T14 after T5 and T7.
scores.rationale: Day-1 tasks, dependency-justified ordering, per-task 'done when' criteria, timed cutover runbook, and spikes with explicit 'changes the plan if' adaptation triggers let a team start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Legal confirms the HIPAA BAA covers every service used. Security completes the HIPAA risk analysis before any PHI enters Azure
Inventory the current system: ... engine channels, outbound vendor endpoints ... Each item marked migrate / repoint / retire.
log backups shipped and applied every 1 min for 2 weeks ... row counts, plus CHECKSUM_AGG(BINARY_CHECKSUM(*)) over the key tables
The migration keeps exactly one writable copy at any moment ... one-way log shipping and an ordered cutover, and reject syncing in both directions
2 rehearsals in a row: pause ≤15 min, reconciliation passes, rollback ≤10 min ... Start reverse log shipping, cloud → old on-site DB
ExpressRoute 1 Gbps + site-to-site VPN on a different ISP ... Extra latency per page is one round trip on ExpressRoute (~2–10 ms)
Data loss (RPO): ≤5 min ... availability group across zones ... staff use the business continuity extract (at most 15 minutes old)
Entra ID with MFA, plus PIM ... Two break-glass accounts ... Break-glass sign-in tested ... SQL Audit sent to the SIEM
Replay recorded user journeys at 2× peak against a production-sized copy ... Replay a synthetic set of 500 messages. Compare message counts.
quietest hour is Sunday 02:00–04:00 ... App releases are frozen from 2 weeks before cutover to 2 weeks after ... 2 weeks of hypercare
Ask the vendor for a written statement of support for Azure IaaS ... Old disks are wiped to NIST 800-88 after retirement.

traps.evidence: The cloud DB has had log backups shipped and applied every 1 min for 2 weeks ... 3 full rehearsals on a production-sized copy
Writing to both systems risks double bookings (#1) ... keeps exactly one writable copy at any moment
the scheduling test environment contains synthetic data, not copies of real patient data ... No public IPs, enforced by an Azure Policy deny rule
repointing the scheduling inbound and outbound connections to the cloud listener ... Interface engine stays on site
Rewriting the app, changing the database schema, upgrading the app version or changing the user interface during the move

note: An exemplary migration plan: technically precise, single-writer discipline, early risk spikes, rehearsed rollback and honest assumptions; it avoids all traps and concretely addresses every checklist item.
